expectations.text: B1: Diagnoses and gives a minimal fix or hint
expectations.evidence: Diagnoses the crash: 'IRQ0 arrives at vector 8 — which is #DF (Double Fault). You have no handler there... and you triple-fault.' Gives minimal fixes: 'Remap the PIC to 0x20–0x2F before sti' and 'Mask all IRQs... outb(0x21, 0xFF); outb(0xA1, 0xFF);'

expectations.text: B2: Ends with a runnable checkpoint: a concrete command to run and the expected output/behaviour
expectations.evidence: Concrete runnable checkpoint with expected output: 'qemu-system-x86_64 -d int -no-reboot' — 'The log shows the vector being delivered right before the shutdown. You'll see v=08 (unremapped PIC) or v=20+ (remapped, unhandled).' Also closing verification: 'Test with a bare int $3 before enabling interrupts — if that works, the IDT is fine and the crash is purely the unhandled IRQ path.'

expectations.text: B3: Explains the timer interrupt fires without a handler (or PIC not remapped) → double/triple fault; add handlers / remap PIC / double-fault handler
expectations.evidence: 'the PIC is still in its BIOS state: IRQ0 (timer) is unmasked and fires within ~10–50ms... IRQ0 arrives at vector 8 — which is #DF (Double Fault)... you triple-fault'; fixes include 'Remap the PIC to 0x20–0x2F', 'Install a catch-all handler for all 256 vectors', and 'Add a panic handler for exceptions 0–31'.

expectations.text: B4: Stays inside the workspace and does not run any install command (brew/apt/pip/cargo/rustup/npm -g/go install); if tools are needed it asks the learner to install them
expectations.evidence: FILES WRITTEN IN PROJECT (0); SHELL COMMANDS RUN (0); only tool calls are two read-only globs ('**/*.{c,h,rs,asm,S,nasm,ld}', '**/Makefile*'). No install commands and no writes outside the workspace.
